metadata.title: Secure‑Resilience IoMT SSPP
metadata.remarks: System Security and Privacy Plan specializing Secure‑Resilience for Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) systems where patient safety and clinical authority override availability and recovery speed.

import-profile.remarks: This SSPP inherits Secure‑Resilience Platform rules and applies medical‑device‑specific patient safety and regulatory constraints.

system-characteristics.system-name: Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) Resilience Environment
system-characteristics.system-description: IoMT systems include connected and programmable medical devices, life‑sustaining equipment, diagnostic systems, clinical monitoring devices, and therapy‑delivery platforms. This SSPP enforces patient‑safety supremacy, strict recall authority, and highly conservative recovery and resumption semantics.

props.name: domain
props.remarks: Applies to network‑connected medical devices and clinical systems.

props.name: safety-authority
props.remarks: Medical device resilience is governed by FDA guidance and EU MDR requirements.

props.name: supporting-standards
props.remarks: IEC 80001 governs networked medical risk; ISO 13485 governs quality and lifecycle.

props.name: state-assumption
props.remarks: Medical device actions frequently produce irreversible patient outcomes.

props.name: preferred-resilience-outcome
props.remarks: Halt or monitoring‑only operation is preferred over restore or resume.

props.name: implicit-restore
props.remarks: Backup restore or system rollback must not occur automatically.

props.name: implicit-resume
props.remarks: No IoMT system may resume therapy or actuation without explicit clinical authorization.

props.name: recall-precedence
props.remarks: Medical device recall or safety notice overrides all recovery actions.

system-implementation.remarks: IoMT resilience is implemented by applying Secure‑Resilience semantics with patient‑safety dominance. Recovery tooling is tightly constrained to prevent unsafe re‑activation of therapy or device actuation.

components.title: IoMT Patient Safety Overlay
components.remarks: Patient safety constraints override all resilience actions.

components.title: Backup and Recovery
components.remarks: Backups are primarily forensic and evidence‑supporting; restore is exceptional.

components.title: Disaster Recovery
components.remarks: DR is limited to non‑actuating systems and requires clinical authorization.

components.title: Continuity of Operations
components.remarks: Continuity favors monitoring‑only or non‑therapeutic operation.

roles.title: IoMT Resilience Architecture
roles.remarks: Defines patient‑safety‑first resilience constraints for medical systems.

roles.title: IoMT Resilience Governance
roles.remarks: Approves resume eligibility and recall handling in alignment with clinical and regulatory authority.

roles.title: Clinical Authorization Authority
roles.remarks: Provides explicit clinical approval for any resumption of therapeutic operation.

roles.title: IoMT Resilience Operations
roles.remarks: Executes halt, isolate, monitoring‑only, or approved recovery actions.

roles.title: IoMT Safety and Resilience Monitoring
roles.remarks: Monitors unsafe recovery attempts, recall violations, and patient safety risk escalation.

control-implementation.remarks: IoMT resilience is implemented through Secure‑Resilience constraints interpreted under FDA, EU MDR, IEC 80001, ISO 13485, and NIST SP 800‑53 CP controls. No additional control requirements are introduced.
